disposalInstruction: Rinse and remove the cap. Place in the dry/recyclable waste bin. Do not crush if your municipality sorts by shape.
specialNotes: PET #1 plastic. Rinsing prevents liquid contamination of paper bales.

disposalInstruction: Rinse thoroughly and place in the dry waste bin. Do not mix with ceramics or broken glass, as they are processed differently.
specialNotes: Infinitely recyclable container glass.

disposalInstruction: Rinse out any residue and place in the dry/recyclable bin. Cans do not need to be crushed unless your local rules ask for it.
specialNotes: Infinitely recyclable aluminum alloy.

disposalInstruction: Rinse and place in the dry waste bin. Sharp edges should be folded inward if possible.
specialNotes: Steel food cans separated easily by magnetic reclamation sorting.

disposalInstruction: Flatten the box and remove any tape or labels if possible. Place in the dry/paper recyclable bin.
specialNotes: Keep dry. Wet cardboard degrades pulp quality.

disposalInstruction: Keep dry and place in the paper recycling bin. Bundle with string if your collection point requires it.
specialNotes: Recyclable newsprint pulp.

disposalInstruction: Rinse and remove the lid (lids often need separate disposal). Place the jar in the dry waste bin.
specialNotes: Remove metal lids to allow separate magnetic and optical separation.

disposalInstruction: Rinse off food residue and check for a recycling symbol. Place in the dry/recyclable bin.
specialNotes: Rigid plastics #1, #2, #5 are commonly accepted curbside.

disposalInstruction: Most paper cups have a plastic lining and are not accepted by standard recycling. Dispose of in general waste unless your facility explicitly accepts them.
specialNotes: Polyethylene lining prevents standard paper repulping.

disposalInstruction: Thin plastic bags jam recycling machinery. Reuse if possible, otherwise dispose of in general waste or a designated soft-plastics drop-off point.
specialNotes: Soft film plastics tangle automated sorting spinning axles.

disposalInstruction: Place in the wet/organic waste bin or a home compost pile.
specialNotes: Nutrient-rich biodegradable biomass.

disposalInstruction: Place in the wet/organic waste bin or compost. Avoid mixing with plastic packaging.
specialNotes: Ideal for vermiculture, aerobic compost, or municipal digesters.

disposalInstruction: Scrape into the wet/organic waste bin. Avoid disposing of large quantities of liquid food waste down drains.
specialNotes: Drain excess gravy/liquid before dumping.

disposalInstruction: Most tea bags can go in organic waste, but check for plastic mesh in premium bags first — if plastic is present, remove it and discard separately.
specialNotes: Remove staple wire if present.

disposalInstruction: Place in the wet/organic waste bin or use directly as garden compost.
specialNotes: High nitrogen soil amendment and odor neutralizer.

disposalInstruction: Place in the wet/organic waste bin or crush and add to compost/soil.
specialNotes: Rich in calcium carbonate.

disposalInstruction: Place leaves, grass clippings, and small branches in the organic/green waste bin or compost pile.
specialNotes: Yard trimmings generate high-quality leaf mulch.

disposalInstruction: Do not place in regular bins. Drop off at a designated e-waste collection center or authorized electronics retailer.
specialNotes: Contains recoverable gold, silver, copper, and critical minerals.

disposalInstruction: Take to a certified e-waste recycler. Many manufacturers also offer take-back programs.
specialNotes: Wipe personal hard drive before drop-off.

disposalInstruction: Never dispose of batteries in general waste. Drop off at a battery collection point or e-waste facility.
specialNotes: Tape terminals with clear adhesive tape to prevent short circuits.

disposalInstruction: Take to an e-waste collection point; cables contain recoverable metals and should not go in general waste.
specialNotes: Copper wiring can be stripped and melted down for re-manufacture.

disposalInstruction: CFL bulbs contain trace mercury. Do not break or bin normally — take to an e-waste or hazardous waste collection point.
specialNotes: If broken, ventilate room immediately and avoid vacuuming powder.

disposalInstruction: Take to an e-waste collection point rather than the general bin, as they contain recoverable electronic components.
specialNotes: Contains microchip drivers and diodes.

disposalInstruction: Remove batteries first (dispose separately), then take the remote to an e-waste collection point.
specialNotes: Separate alkaline/lithium batteries before drop-off.

disposalInstruction: Do not pour leftover paint down drains or into general waste. Let it dry fully if water-based, then check local hazardous waste drop-off guidelines.
specialNotes: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) contaminate municipal water runoff.

disposalInstruction: Never reuse or rinse into open drains. Take to a hazardous waste collection facility.
specialNotes: Toxic to aquatic life and groundwater aquifers.

disposalInstruction: Do not flush or bin loose. Return to a pharmacy take-back program or a designated medical waste drop-off.
specialNotes: Flushing pharmaceuticals bypasses wastewater treatment plants.

disposalInstruction: Place in a puncture-proof container and take to a medical waste or hazardous waste collection point. Never place loose in regular bins.
specialNotes: Sharps injury biohazard to sanitation workers.

disposalInstruction: Never pour down drains or onto soil. Take to an auto shop or hazardous waste facility that accepts used oil.
specialNotes: One liter of motor oil can contaminate 1 million liters of drinking water.

disposalInstruction: Most curbside programs do not accept styrofoam. Dispose of in general waste unless a specialty drop-off is available near you.
specialNotes: Expanded polystyrene (#6) breaks into microplastic beads in sorting plants.

disposalInstruction: Ensure it is fully extinguished, then dispose of in general waste. Never discard on the ground due to toxic residue leaching into soil.
specialNotes: Cellulose acetate filters take up to 10 years to degrade, releasing nicotine and heavy metals.
